profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.jobTitle: Senior Data Engineer / Software Engineer - (PEPFAR PROGRAM)
profile.summary:
Question: What’s the difference between an introverted data engineer and an extroverted one?
Answer: The extrovert stares at your logs instead of your shoes.

I build systems that make data move — reliably, securely, and fast. From global health analytics to fintech pipelines, I love turning messy, chaotic information into something elegant, scalable, and insightful.

Yes, I can write the Python and SQL that keep an analytics platform alive, but what really drives me is solving problems end-to-end — designing the data model, optimizing transformations, deploying architecture, and weaving the story behind the numbers.

Over the past decade I’ve architected platforms used in 40+ countries, integrated LLMs into data workflows, and built real-time analytics systems that actually stay up. My approach blends engineering rigor with curiosity, creativity, and the occasional cup of strong coffee.

I believe great data engineering is part science, part storytelling — and that the best solutions start with good questions (and maybe good food).

If you’re a fellow data tinkerer, ML explorer, or someone who appreciates a clever pipeline or a clever pun, let’s connect.

positions.title: Senior Data Engineer / Software Engineer - (PEPFAR PROGRAM)
positions.description:
•  Architected scalable data and analytics infrastructure for PEPFAR’s global health platform, leveraging Microsoft Fabric, Spark, and AWS to process and visualize international health program data.
•  Built and deployed containerized Flask APIs and CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions + Docker) to automate computational workflows across 45+ countries.
•  Integrated AI/LLM-powered chatbots into analytics dashboards, enabling natural-language queries for health analysts and reducing reporting turnaround by 60%.
•  Partnered with Data Scientists and Engineers to design data models, APIs, and R packages, ensuring reliability, validation, and audit compliance across all datasets.
•  Led GitHub DevOps lifecycle: branching, pull requests, and automated quality gates to standardize deployment pipelines across teams.
•  Operated enterprise Shiny environments and automated reproducible reporting (RMarkdown/Quarto) for internal and client deliverables.

Key Tools: Python, SQL, Spark, Microsoft Fabric, AWS, Docker, Flask, CI/CD, R, GitHub Actions, Data Modeling, LLM Integration

positions.title: Director of Data Engineering & Analytics
positions.description:
•  Directed the design and implementation of the TLC’s data warehouse and analytics platform, processing 100M+ annual trip records for NYC’s for-hire industry.
•  Engineered parallelized ETL pipelines (R MapReduce) and ClickHouse/Postgres data models, achieving a 400–500% improvement in reporting speeds.
•  Developed public dashboards and rapid prototypes (R Shiny, Tableau) including a Driver Income Calculator used by 180,000+ drivers citywide.
•  Applied machine learning (regression, random forest, clustering) to optimize demand forecasting, enforcement prioritization, and 311 complaint categorization.
•  Led the data analysis for landmark policy initiatives, including NYC’s first rideshare pay floor and vehicle cap.
•  Built an internal data culture through documentation, mentorship, and an agency-wide analytics blog.

Key Tools: R, Python, SQL, Postgres, ClickHouse, Spark, Tableau, Data Warehousing, Machine Learning, R Shiny

positions.title: Data & Analytics Manager
positions.description:
• Defined KPIs and automated Python, R and SQL scripts to produce internal and public-facing metrics. 
• Designed schema and managed Postgres and ClickHouse databases. 
• Implemented parallelization in R and SQL scripting jobs that lead to a 400% increase in reporting speeds. 
• Prototyped and built a driver income calculator which is utilized by over 180,000 taxi drivers in New York City. 
• Built and released an R-Shiny-based public dashboard, the TLC Data Hub, which showcases taxi KPIs and trends.
• Spearheaded landmark driver income study, which led to the first national vehicle cap on ridesharing companies, as 
well as the first national requirements on minimum driver pay for over 180,000 drivers. 
• Applied regression and random forest models to predict taxi volume and k-means clustering to improve 311 
complaint categories for taxis

positions.title: Data and Evaluation Manager
positions.description:
•	Data Warehousing: Oversaw and managed six databases to track outcomes and reporting to assist low-income New Yorkers in gaining access to banking services.
•	Analytics: Developed evaluation protocols and analytical tools for testing program models.
•	Statistics: Aided with studies on financial stress as a predictor of counseling outcomes.
•	Reporting: Provided quantitative and qualitative assistance for the Healthy Aging Study, a qualitative report recommending resource upgrades for senior citizens in Far Rockaway.

positions.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant
positions.description:
•	Analytics: Designed and administered surveys on financial counseling outcomes.
•	Evaluation: Developed evaluation protocols for testing efficacy of interventions for all programs.

positions.title: Assistant to the Executive Director
positions.description:
Worth Motorcycle Company, Inc. is a not-for-profit organization whose aim is to impart at-risk youth and marginalized young people with the various social and professional competencies required to excel within the specialized field of vintage European motorcycle restoration.

I worked with the executive director, to plan fund-raisers, construct websites, and lay the empirical foundation for the organization's model of aid for at-risk youth.
